newsitem.title: UK: High costs threat to Lloyd's of London -agent.
newsitem.headline: High costs threat to Lloyd's of London -agent.

text.p: High costs levied by managing agents in particular have eroded Lloyds of London's competitiveness and should be reduced, an agency representing the insurance market's backers, known as Names, said on Thursday.

"These costs have grown substantially over the last 20 years and have destroyed any competitive position that Lloyd's had in relation to its competitors in the 1960s and 1970s," members' agent Christie Brockbank Shipton (CBS) said in its September newsletter.

Around 40 percent of a Name's gross return is lost in one form or another to Lloyd's and market agents, CBS said, adding that Names have done little or nothing to challenge the charges, despite general recognition in the market that they are too high.
The largest single element of costs charged by agents is the approximately 15 percent taken by managing agents as a profit commission on Names' profits, CBS said.
"Unless something is done to reduce the costs for Names and corporate investors then Lloyd's is in danger of becoming an unattractive investment," it added.
"These are quite astonishing figures and bear no comparison with other forms of business let alone the costs that shareholders are required to bear as investors in insurance company stocks."

CBS said that Lloyd's should create a climate in which market forces could drive down costs, while Names' representative bodies and others should bring pressure to bear on syndicates and managing agents to cut charges.
It also called for an end to managing agents and syndicates charging costs separately.
The problem of costs should not be ignored, CBS said, adding, "it is Lloyd's collective problem which will continue to hinder Lloyd's recovery until something is done about it."
